newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD mulls stake in small Polish bank BWE.
newsitem.headline: EBRD mulls stake in small Polish bank BWE.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is mulling a stake in Polish Bank Wschodnio-Europejski SA (BWE), possibly this year, a source close to the EBRD said on Tuesday.

"EBRD is looking at a lot of Polish banks and on (BWE) bank there is a consideration at the moment. It's at a very early stage but there is a possibility there could be an investment (in BWE)," said an official, who declined to be named.
The source said the stake could be taken in 1997 but it was too early to give other.
BWE's president Ryszard Pidek said the bank was considering a share issue, but declined to say whether the issue would be earmarked for the EBRD.
"We are planning to raise the share capital at the next shareholders meeting planned for late March or early April, but I can't give details," he told Reuters.
Pidek also said BWE was considering entering the main market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange, but said it depended on the situation on the bourse when the entry would take place.

BWE is 70 percent-owned by privately held Polish trader Bartimpex which specialises in barter trade in fuels and farm products with former Soviet Union states. The state treasury has eight percent and the remaining shareholders have less than five percent each.
The bank had a balance sheet total of 672.2 million zlotys in 1996. It netted 20.2 million zlotys last year.
